From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: SLO & Private/VPC performance qualification for Acme Health

Thanks for the productive demo today — quick recap and proposed next steps on the performance/SLO side so we can size the Private/VPC deployment correctly.

Key SLOs you asked us to qualify:
- Latency: p95 end-to-end <= 150ms for text generation (single-turn), with streaming token flush latencies <= 50ms
- Throughput: baseline target 500 requests/sec for typical prompt sizes (avg 350 tokens in, 200 tokens out)
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent sessions (many will be streaming)
- Cold-start: warmup time targeting < 2s for a model swap event

Private deployment specifics we need to validate:
- Network path: we'll be connecting via VPC peering or site-to-site VPN into your VPC (please confirm preferred path)
- Egress: are there restrictions on outbound IP ranges or strict egress whitelisting?
- Internal latency budget: you mentioned <20ms from your app tier to the inference host — we need a traceroute/latency sample to confirm feasibility
- Streaming: TLS connection reuse and server push — recommend keeping keepalive > 60s for streaming sessions

Attachments: attached a draft mutual_action_plan.pdf and a short network_checker_instructions.txt to run basic connectivity checks.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sylvia/Tom: share preferred connectivity (VPC peering or VPN) and a short window to run network checks (traceroute, ping, sample payload RTT).
2) Acme: confirm egress whitelist IPs or let us know if you require static NAT egress.
3) Laura/Monica: we'll prepare an environment with a representative model and run a 30-minute throughput/concurrency test once we have connectivity.
4) Schedule a 45-minute follow-up on Friday to review test results and any tuning.

If any of the SLO targets above are off, flag them here and we can recalibrate.

—Aditya

Hi Sylvia — thanks for confirming the VPN path. A few technical notes and what we'll need from your infra team to make the tests meaningful: 

Network checklist (what we typically validate):
- Traceroute + 10 pings from app host to proposed inference subnet (please run both UDP and TCP where possible)
- One sample 1KB request/response RTT and a streaming 1-token-per-30ms test for ~30s to observe flush behavior
- MTU check (we've seen fragmentation affect streaming latency)
- Confirm NAT or no-NAT on egress; if you use NAT, please provide mapped public IPs for whitelisting
- Any IPS/IDS in-line that might buffer or inspect streaming payloads (these commonly add latency spikes)

Sizing and expected performance notes:
- For your target of p95 <=150ms and avg prompt sizes, we recommend starting with 4 x g5.12xlarge equivalents for the model container (we'll provide a more detailed perf profile after baseline tests).
- Bandwidth: ensure at least 1 Gbps sustained between app tier and inference subnet for the 500 req/s target (concurrency 200 streaming).
- We will run a shadow load test: ramp to 200 concurrent streams over 15 minutes, then a 30-minute throughput run at 500 req/s. We instrument token-level latencies and end-to-end RTT.

Deliverables after the test run:
- CSV of per-request latencies, p50/p95/p99, and token flush times
- A short diagnostics trailer with traceroutes and packet capture samples (pcap) if requested
- Recommended tuning (keepalive, TCP tuning, ML VM flags) and a suggested infrastructure footprint for production

If you can run the checks tomorrow morning, we'll stand by and collect results. We'll also provision a short-lived test environment in our dedicated sandbox VPC and provide the egress IPs to whitelist (they'll be static for the test window).

—Laura
